# ADHD foreningen

ADHD foreningen is a Danish patient organization for people with ADHD (attention deficit hyperactivity disorder). It is documented in the corpus as one of the bodies represented on the steering group ("styregruppen") of the ADHD-databasen, a Danish national health quality database that monitors the assessment and treatment of ADHD in children and young people under 18 [^src1][^src2].

The organization appears under two slightly different name forms across the source documents: "ADHD foreningen" (without hyphen) on page 41 of the 2023 report [^src1], and "ADHD-foreningen" (with hyphen) on page 61 of the 2024 report [^src2]. Both refer to the same national patient association and are treated here as one entity.

According to the surrounding documentation, the ADHD-databasen steering group is composed of chief physicians, medical specialists, psychologists, nurses, epidemiologists, and representatives of relatives from across Denmark, and it draws membership from all five Danish regions, relevant professional societies, patient organizations, and the Danish Institute for Quality and Accreditation in Healthcare (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) [^src1][^src2]. ADHD foreningen's role in this structure situates it as the patient-voice representative within a database that tracks statistics on children, young people, and — in later data — adults undergoing ADHD assessment and treatment, including data on educational outcomes such as lower rates of passing the Danish primary school leaving exam ("folkeskolens afgangsprøve") before age 17 among children with ADHD compared to the general population [^src1].

No specific relationships or claims involving ADHD foreningen are recorded beyond its inclusion in the steering group context, and no timeline events are documented for this entity in the corpus.
